texts.preamble: M/S. K.G.N. Chicken And Mutton vs State Of Gujarat on 5 May, 2023 Author: Vaibhavi D. Nanavati Bench: Vaibhavi D. Nanavati C/Sca/5063/2023 Order
texts.facts: 3. The petitioners herein are a group of persons carrying out business of selling live poultry and mutton slaughtered in government dedicated slaughter house since past 20-25 years in the Ved Road area in Surat. It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioners herein are in receipt of valid license issued by the respondent Nos. 2 to 4 vide various certificates to carry on the business of poultry selling and selling slaughtered mutton. The petitioners have placed reliance on the said license, which is produced at Annexure "B". 4. The petitioners herein are constrained to approach this Court because of issuance of show-cause notice by respondent Nos.3 and 4, which is duly produced at Annexure "A", under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards (Licensing And Registration of Food Businesses), Regulations, 2011.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned advocates appearing for the respective parties have jointly submitted that the reliefs, as prayed for by the petitioners, would be governed by the order dated 11.04.2023 passed by the Division Bench in Civil Application (For Direction) No.10 of 2023 in Writ Petition (PIL) No. 133 of 2021 and connected Civil Applications. wherein Para-6 reads thus: "6. All the meat shops and slaughter houses which are closed by the authorities for the reason that they have failed to comply with the licencing and regulatory norms, food and safety standards, pollution control requirements and for any such other legal considerations including non-observance of hygiene imperatives, could hardly be permitted to be reopened on spacious grounds, unless they become fully compliant of such norms and regulations. 6.4 It is also observed that if any such application is made by any shop owner or vendor, it shall be dealt with expeditiously without booking delay."
texts.respondent_arguments: 5. Learned advocates appearing for the respective parties have jointly submitted that the reliefs, as prayed for by the petitioners, would be governed by the order dated 11.04.2023 passed by the Division Bench in Civil Application (For Direction) No.10 of 2023 in Writ Petition (PIL) No. 133 of 2021 and connected Civil Applications.

All the meat shops and slaughter houses which are closed by the authorities for the reason that they have failed to comply with the licencing and regulatory norms, food and safety standards, pollution control requirements and for any such other legal considerations including non-observance of hygiene imperatives, could hardly be permitted to be reopened on spacious grounds, unless they become fully compliant of such norms and regulations. 6.4 It is also observed that if any such application is made by any shop owner or vendor, it shall be dealt with expeditiously without booking delay."
